Unguided natural selection may explain practical cognition but gives insufficient reason to expect minds capable of reliable quantum physics, metaphysics, and philosophical intuition.
This supplies the evolutionary-reliability component of the pro case by contrasting survival-oriented selection with the unexpectedly broad truth-seeking capacities of human reason.

Max grants that navigation and food acquisition could favor reasoning but contends that abstract science, metaphysics, introspection, and the intuitions used in philosophy exceed those adaptive demands.
